title: Personal Agent — user.workflow_playbooks Record
description: Schema for a single record in the user.workflow_playbooks pack (#8 of 14): the recurring action sequences the subject runs to get work done — the repeatable 'how I actually do X' patterns surfaced from sessions, where the order, entry conditions, and per-step checks matter as much as the outcome (WorkflowPattern node). Each record extends the unified base record via allOf $ref to ./record.base.schema.json and narrows record_type to this pack's three types. Routed from WorkflowPatternCandidate (see ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §6 routing) and linked to deliverables via the `produces` edge (WorkflowPattern → Artifact | ArtifactPolicy). Gate G4 applies: describe the observed sequence of actions, not guessed intent. Pack definition: ../spec/03-pack-catalog.md (user.workflow_playbooks); base record: ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §7. (구 코드명: t08.)

record_type.description: Workflow-playbook record kind. WorkflowRecord = a named recurring activity captured at a high level (e.g. 'how I review a PR', 'how I scope a new spec') where the canonical `statement` summarizes the pattern and details live in optional fields. StepSequenceRecord = the same activity captured as an explicit ordered sequence of steps (the `steps` array is the substance), used when order/dependency is the point. PlaybookRecord = a triggered, branchy procedure with named entry conditions and decision points — the 'when this situation, run this play' form (e.g. incident response, release checklist) that compiles most directly into runtime behavior.

workflow_kind.description: Coarse classification of the activity this playbook governs, used for retrieval and for matching a task to the right sequence. Optional; the base `statement` stays canonical.

trigger.description: For PlaybookRecord (and optionally others): the observed situation/entry condition that should cause the runtime to run this playbook, in behavioral terms (e.g. 'when a PR touches the schema', 'when an alert fires for prod'). Refines the required base `scope` into a checkable antecedent without weakening it (Gate G2).

order.description: 1-based position of the step in the sequence.

action.description: The action taken at this step, in behavioral language (e.g. 'read the failing test first', 'draft the summary before the body').

check.description: Optional per-step gate/verification the subject applies before moving on (e.g. 'confirm scope is non-empty', 'all tests green').

optional.description: If true, the step may be skipped when its context does not apply. Defaults to false (treated as required within scope).

steps.description: For StepSequenceRecord/PlaybookRecord: the ordered steps of the sequence. The substance of a sequence record; refines the canonical base `statement` into individually checkable actions an evaluator can score, rather than replacing it.

preconditions.description: What must hold before the playbook starts (e.g. ['branch is up to date', 'reproduction exists']). Distinct from `trigger` (what activates it) — these are entry requirements that gate the first step.

produces_artifacts.description: Deliverables the workflow yields (e.g. ['review board', 'postmortem doc']). Mirrors the graph `produces` edge (WorkflowPattern → Artifact | ArtifactPolicy); use ids/refs where an ArtifactPolicy record in user.artifact_policy governs the format.

applies_to_tasks.description: Task kinds/contexts where this playbook is in effect (e.g. ['code review', 'spec authoring', 'incident triage']). Narrows the required base `scope` into checkable surfaces; complements base `linked_projects`/`linked_domains`.

decision_points.description: Branch/judgment points inside the sequence where the path depends on a condition (e.g. 'if the diff is risky, request a second reviewer'). Surfaces where the workflow defers to a DecisionPolicy or BoundaryRule rather than proceeding mechanically.

enforcement.description: How firmly the runtime should follow this sequence. strict = always run in order within scope; preferred = follow unless overridden; default = a starting template a later cue can adapt; situational = only when the trigger context matches. Distinct from `confidence` (evidence strength), which measures how well-supported the playbook is, not how hard it binds.

$comment: Required fields are inherited unchanged from record.base.schema.json (id, record_type, label, statement, evidence_refs, confidence, scope, review_status, sensitivity, created_at, updated_at); only record_type is constrained here. All fields added by this pack are OPTIONAL — required = base required + record_type, per the pack-focus rule. Base validation still applies: evidence_refs ≥ 1 (G1), non-empty scope (G2), counterexamples required when confidence < 0.7, exception_rules required when sensitivity ∈ {sensitive, restricted}. Display aliases for `statement`: a UI may show 'playbook'/'workflow_steps', but the stored canonical field is `statement` (deprecated bare `instruction`). record_type is constrained to the three user.workflow_playbooks types; routed from WorkflowPatternCandidate (spec/01-kernel-schema.md §6). For StepSequenceRecord/PlaybookRecord the `steps` array refines `statement`; produces_artifacts mirrors the `produces` edge to user.artifact_policy (구 코드명 t08).
